questions.question_text: Evaluate $4^{-3}$, giving your answer as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Read the negative index as making the value negative, evaluating $-4^{3}$ instead of taking the reciprocal.
Multiplied the base by the index, using $4\times 3=12$ instead of $4^{3}=64$.
Took the reciprocal correctly but also carried the minus sign from the index into the answer.

questions.question_text: Write $7^{-5}$ with a positive index. Do not evaluate.

options.why: Swapped the base and the index when writing the reciprocal.
Dropped the negative sign, treating the index as if it were already positive.
Took the reciprocal and also made the expression negative because of the negative index.
Swapped the base and the index while moving the power out of the denominator.
Made the whole expression negative instead of making the index negative.
Made the index negative but left the power in the denominator, undoing the change.

questions.question_text: Write $\frac{1}{32}$ as a power of $2$ with a negative index.

options.why: Swapped the base and the index after finding that $32=2^{5}$.
Found the power of $2$ but left the index positive, giving $32$ rather than $\frac{1}{32}$.
Made the value negative instead of taking the reciprocal of $2^{5}$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate $\frac{1}{2^{-5}}$, giving your answer as a basic numeral.

options.why: Rewrote $2^{-5}$ as $\frac{1}{2^{5}}$ but ignored that it already sits in a denominator.
Moved the power up to the numerator but kept the minus sign as part of the value.
Multiplied the base by the index, using $2\times 5=10$ instead of $2^{5}=32$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate $7\times 3^{-2}$, giving your answer as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Applied the negative index to the whole product, reciprocating $7\times 9=63$ as well as the power.
Formed $\frac{7}{9}$ and then reciprocated it, applying the negative index a second time.
Read $3^{-2}$ as $-3^{2}=-9$, then multiplied by $7$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate $\frac{5^{3}}{5^{6}}$, giving your answer as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Subtracted the indices the wrong way round, using $6-3$ to get $5^{3}$.
Divided the indices, using $6\div 3=2$ instead of subtracting them.
Reached $5^{-3}$ then read the negative index as making the value negative.

questions.question_text: Evaluate $(-3)^{-2}$, giving your answer as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Left the minus sign outside the power, working with $-3^{-2}$ instead of $(-3)^{-2}$.
Squared $-3$ to get $9$ but attached the minus sign from the index instead of taking the reciprocal.
Multiplied the base by the index, using $3\times 2=6$ instead of $(-3)^{2}=9$.

questions.question_text: Which of these has the smallest value: $2^{-5}$, $3^{-3}$, $5^{-2}$ or $10^{-1}$?

options.why: Compared the denominators $27$ and $32$ and chose the smaller denominator as the smaller fraction.
Compared the indices only, reading $-2$ as smaller than $-1$ without evaluating the other powers.
Assumed the largest base always gives the smallest value once the index is negative.

questions.solution_text:
$2^{-5}=\frac{1}{32}$
$3^{-3}=\frac{1}{27}$
$5^{-2}=\frac{1}{25}$
$10^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}$
The numerators are all $1$, so the largest denominator gives the smallest value.
The smallest is $2^{-5}$.

questions.question_text: Find the value of $n$ so that $2^{n}=\frac{1}{64}$.

options.why: Found that $64=2^{6}$ but left the index positive, which gives $64$ rather than $\frac{1}{64}$.
Counted the powers of $2$ one short, treating $2^{5}=32$ as $64$.
Used the number $64$ itself as the index instead of the power of $2$ that makes it.
